implemented_capabilities.capability: npm package-lock parsing into dependency graph (Node resolution semantics, depth BFS, hostile-input limits)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Converts lockfileVersion 2/3 into Dep nodes and REQUIRES edges mirroring npm arborist/Node resolution, computes shortest depth from root, and sanitises names/ranges/versions with size and entry caps (6000 entries, 50k edges).

implemented_capabilities.capability: Temporal exposure window for a semver range admitting a malicious version (ADMITS fromT/toT)
implemented_capabilities.notes: admitWindow computes [fromT,toT) during which a declared range would have resolved to the bad version, closing the window when a higher satisfying version is published or the bad one is removed. Stored as ADMITS edge properties and queried with 'at' time travel.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Tiered incident exposure at a point in time (LOCKED / WOULD_PULL / MAINTAINER / CLEAN)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Runs parameterised Cypher via GRAPH.RO_QUERY and merges tiers per repo, honouring a 'lockfile cannot predate the version it locks' rule; also computes 'minutes ahead of advisory'.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Dependency path explanation (shortest lockfile chain from repo root to locked/admitting entry)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Cypher shortestPath((root)-[:REQUIRES*0..]->(x)) limited to 3 shallowest entries and memoised for the demo graphs; returns chain, range, hops.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Remediation drafting (npm overrides pinning to highest clean version live at time T)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Computes version-qualified overrides satisfying every affected range, orders steps differently for LOCKED vs WOULD_PULL, and emits a PR body; deterministic code, not an LLM.
Builds a PKG_DEPENDS package projection and runs FalkorDB's built-in CALL algo.pageRank, then sums pagerank per maintainer.

implemented_capabilities.capability: LLM narrative claim guard (verifies entities, numbers and evidence citations in LLM text against tool evidence)
implemented_capabilities.notes: A linear-time single-pass tokenizer extracts npm@version, owner/repo, counts and [E1] citations, then marks each claim ok/flagged against a graph-derived evidence set. The LLM only picks an observation id; narrative text is deterministic.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Deterministic triage playbook with session memory
implemented_capabilities.notes: Async-generator pipeline of registry tools (find_target, suspect_versions, incident_exposure, explain_path, route_owners, draft_remediation, concentration_risk, scanner_view) whose branching depends on graph output; writes :Triage nodes with ASSESSED edges (tier, action remediated/notified/accepted-risk) per anonymous session.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Read-only MCP server exposing graph tools
implemented_capabilities.notes: Stdio MCP server registering all tools except session-scoped recall_triage with readOnlyHint; no raw Cypher tool; results include the exact Cypher that ran.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Multi-provider LLM client with fallback chain, daily cap and outbound allowlist
implemented_capabilities.notes: OpenAI-compatible calls to Groq and Gemini with ordered fallback, 800 calls/day cap, https-only host allowlist, redirect refusal and prompt sanitisation.

graph_models_and_cypher: Nodes: Package, Version, Maintainer, Incident, Advisory, Org, Team, Repo, Dep (one per lockfile entry), Triage. Edges: OF, MAINTAINS, INVOLVES, COMPROMISED, PUBLISHED_BY, FLAGS, PULLS_IN, IN_ORG, OWNED_BY, ROOT, REQUIRES{range,kind}, RESOLVES_TO, ADMITS{range,fromT,toT} (temporal validity window), PKG_DEPENDS, FOR, ASSESSED{tier,action}. Cypher is parameterised ($params) and executed with GRAPH.RO_QUERY for reads; GRAPH.COPY clones a registry graph per scenario; indexes + UNIQUE constraints via CREATE INDEX / constraintCreate; shortestPath with variable-length REQUIRES*0..; UNWIND-batched CREATE; UNION; collect(DISTINCT ...). Uses FalkorDB built-in CALL algo.pageRank (not Neo4j GDS/APOC), so it is FalkorDB-native.
algorithms: admitWindow in server/ingest/admits.ts: semver range admission window [published(bad), min(removedAt, first higher satisfying release)) closing on supersession
safeVersion in server/ingest/admits.ts: highest non-malicious version live at time T satisfying all ranges
parseLockfile in server/ingest/lockfile.ts: Node-style resolve() walking up node_modules, BFS depth from root
EXPLAIN_PATH Cypher shortestPath over REQUIRES edges (server/tools/cypher.ts)
CALL algo.pageRank('Package','PKG_DEPENDS') summed per maintainer for concentration risk (server/ingest/build.ts, CONCENTRATION_RISK)
guard() claim tokenizer and evidence verification (server/agent/guard.ts)
incidentExposure tier merge with LOCKED-since gating (server/tools/registry.ts)
backend_interfaces: Hono routes in server/index.ts: GET /api/health, /api/scenarios, /api/timeline, /api/exposure, /api/plan, /api/stats; POST /api/triage (SSE), /api/ask, /api/analyze, /api/remediate

MCP stdio server (server/mcp.ts) exposing find_target, suspect_versions, incident_exposure, maintainer_blast_radius, explain_path, route_owners, concentration_risk, draft_remediation, scanner_view, filter_exposures
CLI: npm run triage, build:graph, mcp
frontend_interfaces: React 19 SPA in web/src: PasteBox, ExposureTable, PathGraph/PathGraphCanvas (react-force-graph-2d), TimelineScrubber, ScenarioControl, NarrativePanel, FixDrawer, AskBox, ToolFeed/ToolCard, GraphStatsSheet, ExecSummary, ContrastCard
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Deterministic tool-sequencing triage generator (not an LLM planner); an Ask loop (server/agent/ask.ts) lets an LLM call registry tools, with args coerced and capped (str/strs/time) and the server overwriting session. Session memory is persisted as :Triage nodes with ASSESSED edges carrying remediation actions and recalled via recall_triage; recorded LLM picks are replayed from data/replays/*.json. Guard checks every LLM claim against tool evidence before display.
tests_present: 11 files under test/ (admits, api, data, graph, guard, llm, lockfile, mcp, narrate, readme, security) with roughly 124 test()/it() cases, plus ~25 co-located web/src/**/*.test.ts files. Graph tests require a live FalkorDB. Not executed by auditor.
dependency_requirements: FalkorDB server with GRAPH.COPY and algo.pageRank
security_findings: scripts/oracle.ts:18 - execFileSync('npm', [...], {shell: true}) dev-only oracle script; arguments are static but shell:true on a path-derived cwd
server/security.ts:72-100 - outbound fetch is allowlisted (github, npm registry, osv, groq, gemini); redirects refused. Positive control, not a finding
server/graph/client.ts:13 - falls back to hard-coded dev password 'devpass' when REDIS_PASSWORD is unset and NODE_ENV is not production (dev default, not a real secret)
.env.example:8-10 - placeholder passwords only ('change-me'); no real secrets found

server/graph/client.ts:80-83 - explain() builds a 'CYPHER k=v' prefix with JSON.stringify of server-chosen sample values (documented as server-only); falkordb client inlines params so assertSafeParams guards map keys
No eval/exec/pickle/unsafe deserialisation found in server code; all Cypher values travel as $params; graph names are built only from fixed parts plus a hash
start.sh uses redis ACL users pz_ro/pz_rw and hashed default password; no secrets in argv
duplicates_or_overlaps: Supply-chain blast-radius traversal (maintainer/package -> repos), dependency-path explanation, remediation drafting. Overlaps other npm supply-chain / blast-radius repos in the hackathon set (e.g. blast-radius, ghostgraph variants) but is unusually complete on time-windowed exposure.
evidence_drift_relevance: HIGH - ADMITS edges with fromT/toT implement temporal validity closed by supersession (higher release or removal), incidentExposure answers 'as of time T', and guard.ts verifies narrative claims against graph evidence with citation ids.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Small, pure, well-specified temporal-validity and supersession logic (window opens at bad publish and closes on removal or a higher satisfying release) with a companion claim-vs-evidence guard in server/agent/guard.ts; both map directly to evidence-drift windows and claim verification.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: TypeScript source with semver dependency; algorithms are trivially portable to Python (packaging/semver). Query layer needs FalkorDB (already native). No LLM key needed for admits/guard.

strategy_rationale: FalkorDB-native Cypher query set and schema for dependency exposure can be ported as a Software Dependency pack; admitWindow and guard should be re-implemented in Python as shared temporal-validity and claim-verification helpers. The TypeScript server and UI should not be merged directly.
